summary: N. R. Bhatt (1920–2009) was an Indology scholar who held a post at the French Institute of Pondicherry and was a member of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 1966).

N. S. Ramachandra Murthy is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as an Epigraphy Assistant in Andhra Pradesh's Department of Archaeology and Museums and retired as Professor of Indian History and Archaeology at Sri Venkateswara University.

N. S. Ramanuja Tatacharya (1928–2017) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Vice Chancellor of the National Sanskrit University from 1989 to 1994 and worked as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry from around 1989 to 2002.
N. Taher is a history and archaeology scholar who succeeded K. K. Muhammed as head of the Bhopal circle at the Archaeological Survey of India.

N. Veezhinathan, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, earned his PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 under A. Sankaran. He was a research scholar at Deccan College (1960–1963) and was appointed Lecturer in Sanskrit at University of Madras in 1964.

N. Venkataramanayya (1891–1976), who studied under Ferrand E. Corley, was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He served as Reader in Indian History at the University of Madras (attested 1957) and Deputy Director for Epigraphy in Andhra Pradesh's archaeology department.

Nadine Stchoupak (1886–1941) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. After studying at Saint Petersburg State University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, she served as Secretary and Librarian at the Institut de Civilisation Indienne (1927–1939) and taught Sanskrit at EPHE (1931–1937).

Nae Ionescu (1890–1940) was a philosophy and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Bucharest (1908–1912), University of Göttingen (1913–1914), and University of Munich (1915–1919), later holding a post at the University of Bucharest from roughly 1919 to 1938.
Nagin J. Shah (born 1931) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who succeeded Dalsukh Malvania as Acting Director at the L.D. Institute of Indology, a post attested in 1968.

Nalinaksha Dutt (1894–1973), a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, earned doctorates from Calcutta and London. He was Professor of Pali at Judson College, Head of the Pali Department at Calcutta (~1921–1958), and President of The Asiatic Society (1959–1961).

Nalini Balbir is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Colette Caillat. Her career includes posts at CNRS, Sorbonne Nouvelle University, University of Paris, and École Pratique des Hautes Études, where she became Emerita Professor in 2022.

Nalini Devdas is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. She completed her PhD at Concordia University under Leslie Orr (attested 2004) and held an academic post at Carleton University.

Nam-lin Hur is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and completed his doctorate under Helen Hardacre, later serving as a Harvard postdoctoral fellow and professor at the University of British Columbia.

Naman P. Ahuja is an Indology and art history scholar who received his doctorate from SOAS University of London. He was attested in 2018 as Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Namgyal Rinpoche (1931–2003) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Jarvis Baptist Seminary and the University of Michigan, as well as under traditional teachers. He founded the Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery (1965) and Dharma Centre of Canada (1966).

Namio Egami (1906–2002) was a history, archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930), he held a post there (~1948–1967) and later served as Director of the Ancient Orient Museum (~1978–2002).
Namita Das is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed her PhD at Gauhati University under doctoral supervisor Sibnath Sarma.

Namkhai Norbu (1938–2018) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Derge Gonchen, Kuse Serjong Shedra, and Khamdre Shedra. He held academic posts at IsMEO, Southwest Minzu University, and the University of Naples from 1962 to 1992.

Nancy E. Levine (born 1949) is a scholar in Tibetology and anthropology. She has held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, including Associate Professor (attested 1998) and Professor of Anthropology (attested 2026).

Nancy G. Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She holds degrees from Bryn Mawr, Columbia, Chicago, and UC Berkeley, and has held posts at Lawrence University and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.
